Rashi on Sanhedrin 31b:11:1.english: Were struggling - That they became unyielding toward each other.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 31b:14:1.hebrew: אפילו מטבריא לציפורי - אע"פ שישיבת טבריא גדולה משל ציפורי, הלך אחריו לציפורי:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 31b:14:1.english: Even from Tiberias to Tzippori - Even though the academy of Tiberias is greater than that of Tzippori, [one must] follow him to Tzippori.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 31b:16:1.hebrew: והאמר רבי אלעזר - והא חזינן דפליג עלה ר' אלעזר לעיל, ויהיב טעמא למילתיה, דמסתבר טעמא:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 31b:16:1.english: But didn’t Rabbi Elazar say - For behold, we see that Rabbi Elazar disagreed with it above, and gave a reason for his statement, which is a compelling reason.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 31b:16:2.hebrew: היכא דקאמר לוה - ״נלך למקום הוועד״ — כופין אותו וידון כאן, ולא יוציא זה מנה על מנה:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 31b:16:2.english: Where the borrower says - “Let us go to the place of the Assembly” — we compel him and he shall be judged here, so that this one will not spend a maneh to [collect] a maneh.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 31b:17:1.hebrew: מר עוקבא - אב ב"ד הוה, במסכת שבת, בבמה בהמה יוצאה (דף נה.):
Rashi on Sanhedrin 31b:17:1.english: Mar Ukva - He was Head of the Court [Av Beit Din], [as stated] in Tractate Shabbat, in [the chapter entitled] Bameh Behemah Yotzah (daf 55a).

Rashi on Sanhedrin 31b:17:2.hebrew: לדזיו ליה כבר בתיה - כמשה שהוא בן בתיה: למי שמקרין עור פניו כמשה רבינו, שגידלתו בתיה בת פרעה. לשון אחר: כבר ביתיה — כמשה שהוא בן בית, דכתיב (במדבר י״ב:ז׳): ״בכל ביתי נאמן הוא״. לדזיו ליה — על שם שהיה חכם, וכתיב (קהלת ח׳:א׳): ״חכמת אדם תאיר פניו״. ומצאתי בספר הגדה שהיה מר עוקבא בעל תשובה, שנתן עיניו באשה אחת והעלה לבו טינא ונפל בחולי, ואשת איש היתה. לימים נצרכה ללות ממנו, ומתוך דוחקה נתרצית לו, וכבש יצרו ופטרה לשלום, ונתרפא. וכשהיה יוצא לשוק היה נר דולק בראשו מן השמים, ועל שם כך קרי ליה ר' נתן צוציתא במסכת שבת (דף נו:). הכא נמי, להכי כתבו ליה הכי, על שם האור שהיה זורח עליו:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 31b:17:2.english: To him who has light upon him, like the son of Bithiah - Like Moses, who was the son of Bithiah: to one whose facial skin radiated like our teacher Moses, whom Bithiah the daughter of Pharaoh raised. Another explanation: Like a member of His household — like Moses, who was a member of the household, as it is written: “In all My house he is trusted” (Numbers 12:7). “To him who has light upon him” — because he was wise, and it is written: “A man’s wisdom illuminates his face” (Ecclesiastes 8:1). And I found in a book of Aggada that Mar Ukva was a penitent, for he set his eyes on a certain woman, and his heart became inflamed with lust, and he fell ill; and she was a married woman. After some time she needed to borrow from him, and out of her distress she consented to him; but he overcame his inclination and dismissed her in peace, and he was healed. And whenever he would go out to the marketplace, a lamp would shine over his head from Heaven; and on account of this he was called Rabbi Natan Tzutzita in Tractate Shabbat (daf 56b). Here too, for this reason they wrote to him thus, on account of the light that shone upon him.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 31b:17:3.hebrew: עוקבן הבבלי קבל קדמנא - צעק לפנינו, ואמר: "ירמיה אחי העביר עלי את הדרך" — איבד ממני דרך בני אדם, שסירסו; כך שמעתי. וי"א: "העביר עלי את הדרך" — לא נהג עמי כשורה, ועל עסקי ממון היה צועק:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 31b:17:3.english: Ukvan the Babylonian complained before us - He cried out before us and said: "Yirmeyah my brother has removed the way from me" — he deprived me of the way of mankind, in that he castrated him; so I heard. And some say: "He overstepped the path with me" — he did not conduct himself properly with me, and it was concerning monetary matters that he was crying out.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 31b:17:4.english: They said to him - To Yirmeya, to appease him:

Rashi on Sanhedrin 31b:17:5.english: Induce him, and let him see our face in Tiberias - Compel him and obligate him to come here to litigate with him.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 31b:1:1.hebrew: קלתיה - שרפתו. הלכך, מה לה לשקר:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 31b:1:1.english: She could have burned it - She [could have] burned it; therefore, what reason would she have to lie?

Rashi on Sanhedrin 31b:2:1.hebrew: דאיתחזק בבי דינא - שכתוב בו הנפק, לא אלימא איהי לאפקועי מעשה ב"ד:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 31b:2:1.english: That it was ratified in court - That an endorsement of ratification is written on it; she is not powerful enough to nullify an act of the court.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 31b:3:1.hebrew: סימפון - שובר, ויצא מתחת יד לוה כמשפטו:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 31b:3:1.english: A receipt [simfon] - A receipt [shovar]. And [in this case] it emerged from the possession of the borrower, as is customary.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 31b:3:2.hebrew: יתקיים - השטר בחותמיו: יעידו עדים על חתימות ידיהן, וכשר:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 31b:3:2.english: Is ratified - The document [is ratified] by its signatories: witnesses testify about their signatures, and it is valid.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 31b:3:3.hebrew: אין עליו עדים - והרי הוא יוצא מתחת יד שליש, ולא מתחת יד הלוה; הואיל ושניהם מודים שזה מינהו להיות שליש ביניהם — כשר:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 31b:3:3.english: There are no witnesses on it - And behold, it emerges from the possession of a third party, and not from the possession of the debtor; since both of them admit that they appointed this [person] to be a third party between them, [it is] valid.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 31b:3:4.hebrew: או שיצא אחר חיתום שטרות - בתוך שטר המלוה נכתב השובר תחת העדים — כשר, שהרי המלוה עצמו מוחזק בשטרו, ואי לאו דפרעיה, לא הוה שביק למיכתב תברא בגוויה:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 31b:3:4.english: Or if it emerged after the signing of the documents - [If] the receipt was written inside the lender's promissory note beneath the [signatures of the] witnesses, [it is] valid, for the lender himself is in possession of his promissory note, and were it not that [the borrower] paid him, he would not have allowed a receipt to be written inside it.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 31b:5:1.hebrew: עד שיסתתם טענותיו - משמע שאמר בבית דין: ״אין לי לא עדים ולא ראיה״, וחזר ואמר: ״קרבו פלוני ופלוני״, שהיו מזומנין שם, ומתחילה סותר טענותיו לומר: ״אין לי״:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 31b:5:1.english: Until his claims are stopped up - [This] implies that he said in court: “I have neither witnesses nor proof,” and then said: “Come forward, so-and-so and so-and-so,” who were standing ready there, and at first he contradicts his claims by saying: “I have none.”

Rashi on Sanhedrin 31b:6:1.hebrew: הא גופא קשיא - יסתתם טענותיו משמע: מכיון שיסתמו, שוב אין מביא ראיה, ואפילו מצאם לאחר זמן — כרבנן. והדר קתני קרבו, דמשמע: דהאי הוא דלא מייתי, דאפי' רשב"ג מודה בו; אבל מצאם לאחר זמן — מייתי, כרבן שמעון:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 31b:6:1.english: This matter itself is difficult - “His claims are stopped up” implies: Once they are stopped up, he can no longer bring proof, and even if he found them after [some] time — in accordance with the Rabbis. And then it teaches: “Come [so-and-so],” which implies: It is [only] this [case] where he may not bring [them], for even Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel agrees with it; but [if] he found them after [some] time, he may bring [them] — in accordance with Rabban Shimon [ben Gamliel].

Rashi on Sanhedrin 31b:8:1.hebrew: ואמר אין לי עדים - ואפילו מצאן לאחר זמן, אינו סותר — כרבנן:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 31b:8:1.english: And he said: "I have no witnesses" - And even if he found them after [some] time, he does not overturn [the verdict], in accordance with [the view of] the Rabbis.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 31b:8:2.english: A saddlebag - A leather bag in which his father's documents were placed.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 31b:9:1.hebrew: התוקף את חבירו בדין - בעל דין קשה ומטריח את חבירו, ואין רוצה חבירו לדון כאן אלא למקום וועד תלמידי חכמים הרבה, שיהא זה בוש מהם:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 31b:9:1.english: One who attacks his fellow in judgment - [This refers to] a difficult litigant who burdens his fellow, and his fellow does not want to litigate here, but rather [wants to go] to the place of assembly of many Torah scholars, so that this [litigant] will be ashamed before them.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 31b:10:1.hebrew: (ויוציא מנה על מנה - מכאן למתחייב בדין, דלא משלם לאידך יציאותיו, אע"פ שמזקיקו לילך לו לדון בעיר אחרת):
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 31b:10:1.english: (“And [must he] spend a maneh for a maneh?” - From here [it is derived] regarding one who is found liable in court, that he does not pay the other [party] his expenses, even though he compelled him to go litigate with him in another city.)

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 31b:12:1.hebrew: ואם אמר כתבו ותנו לי מאיזה טעם כו' - דוקא היכא דנתעצמו לדון כו' וכפו אותו לדון כאן, אבל בעלמא לא. וכן משמע באיזהו נשך (ב"מ דף סט. ושם) גבי תרי כותאי דעבוד עיסקא, דא"ל: "חזינא דכל בתר דידי קאזיל מר", וקאמר: "כי האי ודאי צריך לאודועי". מיהא יש לדחות, דהכי קאמר: כי האי ודאי צריך לאודועי — אע"פ שאין שואל מאיזה טעם נתחייב צריך לאודועי; אבל בעלמא: אי שאיל — אין, אי לא — לא:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 31b:12:1.english: "And if he said: Write and give me for what reason, etc." - [This applies] specifically where they disputed [where] to litigate, etc., and they compelled him to litigate here, but in general, [the court does] not [need to do so]. And so it is implied in [the chapter entitled] Eizehu Neshekh (Bava Metzia 69a, and there [69b]) regarding two Samaritans who entered into a joint venture, where [one] said to him: "I see that the Master pursues me," and [Rav Pappa] said: "In a case like this, one certainly needs to inform [him]." However, [this proof] can be refuted, for this is what it means: In a case like this, one certainly needs to inform him — [meaning,] even though he does not ask for what reason he was found liable, one needs to inform him; but in general: if he asks, yes, [they must inform him;] if not, no, [they do not].

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 31b:19:1.hebrew: אי ציית ציית - אין לפרש: "אי לא ציית" — שלא תוכלו לכופו, דכ"ש שלא יוכל נשיא לכופו, דהכא שבט והתם מחוקק, ומר עוקבא ריש גולה הוה. אלא מפר"ת: "אי לא ציית" — כגון דאמר: "לב"ד הגדול קאזילנא":
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 31b:19:1.english: “If he listens, he listens” - One should not explain [that] “if he does not listen” [means] that you are unable to coerce him, for all the more so the Nasi would not be able to coerce him, for here [in Babylonia is] the “scepter” and there [in Eretz Yisrael is] the “lawgiver,” and Mar Ukva was the Exilarch. Rather, Rabbeinu Tam explains [that] “if he does not listen” [is referring to a case] such as where he says: “I am going to the Great Court.”

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 31b:2:1.hebrew: וכיון דאיתחזק בבי דינא - פי' הקונטרס: שכתוב בו הנפק. וקשה: דמכל מקום ניהמנה במיגו דאי בעי קלתיה! וי"ל: דאיתחזק בבי דינא — שראוהו בידה, כי ההוא דשילהי מי שמת (ב"ב דף קנט:) שהוחזק כתב ידו בבית דין:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 31b:2:1.english: "And since it was ratified in court" - The Kuntres [Rashi] explained that an endorsement [hanpek] was written upon it. And this is difficult: For nevertheless, she should be deemed credible by virtue of a migo that if she had wanted, she could have burned it! And one can say that "it was ratified in court" [means] that they saw it in her hand, like that [case] at the end of [the chapter] Mi Shemet (Bava Batra 159b), where his handwriting was established in court.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 31b:3:1.hebrew: סמפון שיש עליו עדים - פ"ה: שובר, ויוצא מתחת ידי לוה כמשפטו. ור"ת פירש: דביד הלוה קרוי שובר, וכשהוא יוצא מתחת ידי המלוה קרוי סמפון. ו"יתקיים בחותמיו" — היינו דשיילינא לסהדי אי פריע אי לא פריע, כדאיתא שילהי פ"ק דב"מ (דף):
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 31b:3:1.english: "A receipt [simfon] upon which witnesses [are signed]" - The Kuntres [Rashi] explained: A receipt [shovar], and [in this case] it emerges from the possession of the debtor, as is customary. And Rabbeinu Tam explained that [when it is] in the hand of the debtor, it is called a shovar, and when it emerges from the possession of the creditor, it is called a simfon. And "it is ratified by its signatories" — that is, we ask the witnesses whether [the debt was] repaid or not repaid, as it is stated at the end of the first chapter of Bava Metzia (daf [20b–21a]).

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 31b:3:2.hebrew: אין עליו עדים ויוצא - השטר והסמפונות מתחת ידי שליש כשר — משמע ליה אפילו איתחזק, דומיא דיוצא אחר חיתום שטרות. א"נ יש לפרש: לאו דאין עליו עדים כלל, אלא יש עליו עדים ולא ידעי אי פריע אי לא פריע, ויוצא הסמפונות מתחת ידי שליש:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 31b:3:2.english: “There are no witnesses on it, but it emerged” - [The ruling that when] the promissory note and the receipt emerge from the possession of a third party, [the receipt is] valid — [Rava] understood it [to apply] even if [the note] was ratified [in court], similar to [the case where a receipt] emerges after the signing of the documents. Alternatively, it can be explained: [It does] not [mean] that there are no witnesses on it at all, but rather that there are witnesses on it, but they do not know whether it was repaid or whether it was not repaid, and the receipt emerges from the possession of a third party.
